titulo.texto: Landscape Hall: Mammoth, Obsidian, and Caves

frase_gancho.texto: A femur and tusks from a mammoth, more than ten thousand years old, recall who walked through Morelos before its peoples arrived.

puente_narrativo.texto: Continue to the hall of the peoples of maize and stone and the hall of the Olmec.

guion_corto.texto: The bones that greet you in this hall are more than ten thousand years old. They are a femur and tusks from a mammoth, an animal of the last ice age. The hall is called Landscape, and it tells the story of the ecosystems and geology of Morelos. There are fossils, pieces of obsidian, a volcanic glass used to make sharp edges, and basketry from the caves of El Gallo and La Chagüera. The museum estimates that the region has been inhabited for about six thousand three hundred years before our era. But this hall goes further back: it shows that the territory already existed, with its nature, before the first person arrived. Morelos is a small state, but it brings together mountains, valleys, and warm lowlands.

guion_largo.texto:
The museum in the Palace of Cortés changed its approach when it reopened in two thousand twenty-three. Before, it told history by eras and by famous figures. Now, according to those in charge, it tells who shaped the territory, from the first communities to today, without focusing on great dates or great figures. This hall is the best example of that idea, because it begins with the landscape.

The Landscape Hall speaks of the ecosystems and the geology of Morelos. It is a small state, but it has forests in the highlands of the north and warm lowlands toward the south. That variety of climates explains why there were so many ways of living here.

What draws the most attention are the mammoth remains. There is a femur and tusks more than ten thousand years old. The mammoth is an extinct animal, a relative of the elephants, that lived in the last ice age. When people think about that era, almost no one imagines that these animals passed through what is now Morelos, but these remains show it.

There are also fossils and pieces of obsidian. Obsidian is volcanic glass. It breaks into very sharp flakes, which is why it was a valuable material for making knives and points since prehistory. That it is found in a hall about landscape is no accident: obsidian is born from volcanoes, and Morelos has volcanoes nearby.

Another part of the hall shows basketry from the caves of El Gallo and La Chagüera. Baskets are fragile objects. That they have survived for so long indicates that the caves preserved the materials well. That is why archaeologists are so interested in these sites: they hold things that are almost never preserved in the open air.

Another hall in the museum, Biodiversity, uses infographics to show the endemic flora and fauna of Morelos. Endemic means that it occurs in only one place. The two halls form a pair: one shows what lives in the territory today, and the other, what has left its mark for thousands of years. Fossils, for their part, are remains or traces of living beings that were preserved in rock.

The museum is not yet complete. According to INAH, the archaeology halls, the halls on history from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century, and the halls on anthropology from the twentieth to the twenty-first century are still missing. An epilogue on the shared responsibility of caring for heritage is also missing. At the reopening in two thousand twenty-three, five permanent halls and three temporary exhibitions opened.

If you think about it, a museum of this kind does something that textbooks do not. It puts a real bone in front of you, from an animal that no one has seen alive, and lets you estimate its size by eye.

When you finish, keep one idea with you. Before the kings, the conquistadors, and the governors, there was a landscape that offered water, stone, plants, and animals. Everything else was built on top of that.

texto: Find the mammoth femur and tusks and estimate how big the animal that carried them was
Find the obsidian pieces and notice how the material shines, much like glass
Look at the basketry from the caves and think about how long it was kept safe

texto.pregunta: Myth: Mammoths only lived in the cold lands of the north.
texto.respuesta: Reality: There are mammoth remains in Morelos, and the museum displays a femur and tusks more than ten thousand years old.
